name: Bangkok
operatingHours: BTS Skytrain runs ~5:15 AM–midnight (last trains leave Siam ~12:00 AM); MRT Blue and Purple lines ~5:30–6:00 AM–midnight; Airport Rail Link and SRT Red Line ~5:30 AM–midnight. No overnight trains; use taxis or Grab late at night.
fareInfo: BTS and MRT are separate systems with separate gates and fares: changing between them means exiting and paying again (~80–100 THB for a long trip with a transfer). BTS: 17–47 THB on the core Sukhumvit/Silom lines, up to ~65 THB onto the extensions; pay with a Rabbit card (220 THB incl. 100 THB credit) or a single-journey ticket, bank cards not accepted. MRT Blue: 17–44 THB, Purple 14–42 THB; tap a contactless Visa/Mastercard/UnionPay at the gate or buy a token. Airport Rail Link 15–45 THB and SRT Red Line 12–42 THB also take contactless cards. The 20 THB flat-fare scheme is for registered Thai citizens only; a unified fare cap is planned for 2027.

sights.name: Wat Pho (Temple of the Reclining Buddha)
sights.note: Bangkok's oldest and largest temple complex, home to a 46-metre gilded reclining Buddha and the traditional Thai massage school.

sights.name: The Grand Palace & Temple of the Emerald Buddha
sights.note: The former royal residence, a walled compound of gilded halls that also holds Wat Phra Kaew and its revered Emerald Buddha; strict dress code (covered shoulders and knees).
sights.hours: 8:30 AM–3:30 PM daily (last tickets 3:30 PM); closes for royal ceremonies

sights.name: Wat Arun (Temple of Dawn)
sights.note: Riverside temple whose porcelain-studded central prang glows at sunset; a 5-minute cross-river ferry from Tha Tien pier near Wat Pho.

sights.name: Chatuchak Weekend Market
sights.note: One of the world's largest markets, with 15,000 stalls selling everything from clothes and ceramics to plants and street food; next to MRT Chatuchak Park and BTS Mo Chit.
sights.hours: Sat–Sun ~9:00 AM–6:00 PM (some stalls open Fri evening)

sights.name: Jim Thompson House
sights.note: A cluster of teak houses on a canal, assembled by the American silk entrepreneur who vanished in 1967, filled with his Southeast Asian art; seen by guided tour.

sights.name: Lumpini Park
sights.note: Downtown's big green lung, with a lake for pedal boats, morning tai chi, joggers and wild monitor lizards; free entry.

sights.name: Rajadamnern Muay Thai Stadium
sights.note: Thailand's oldest purpose-built Muay Thai stadium (1945), staging live professional bouts every night of the week.
sights.hours: Fights nightly, starting ~6:00–7:00 PM (card varies by night)

sights.name: Wat Traimit (Temple of the Golden Buddha)
sights.note: Temple at the gateway to Chinatown housing a 5.5-tonne solid gold Buddha, rediscovered under a plaster shell in 1955.

sights.name: King Power Mahanakhon SkyWalk
sights.note: Observation deck atop the pixelated Mahanakhon tower, with a glass-floor tray hanging over the edge 310 metres up; next to BTS Chong Nonsi.

sights.name: The Golden Mount (Wat Saket)
sights.note: A hilltop golden chedi reached by 344 steps spiralling past bells and waterfalls, with a 360-degree view over the old city.

sights.name: SEA LIFE Bangkok Ocean World
sights.note: Large aquarium in the basement of Siam Paragon with a walk-through shark tunnel, penguins and a glass-bottom boat ride.

sights.name: Snake Farm (Queen Saovabha Memorial Institute)
sights.note: Red Cross research institute that milks venomous snakes for antivenom, with live handling shows and a snake museum.
sights.hours: Mon–Fri 9:30 AM–3:30 PM, Sat–Sun 9:30 AM–1:00 PM; shows ~11:00 AM (and ~2:30 PM weekdays)

sights.name: Wat Paknam Phasi Charoen
sights.note: Thonburi temple famed for its giant seated bronze Buddha and a white stupa whose top floor has a glass stupa under a swirling green ceiling mural.

sights.name: Khaosan Road
sights.note: The original backpacker strip: a pedestrianised evening of street bars, pad thai carts, massage chairs and loud music.

sights.name: Yaowarat Road (Chinatown)
sights.note: Chinatown's neon-lit main street, which turns into one of Asia's great street-food strips after dark (seafood, noodles, mango sticky rice).
sights.hours: Street food ~6:00 PM–midnight; many stalls off on Mondays

sights.name: Erawan Shrine
sights.note: Busy Hindu shrine to Brahma at the Ratchaprasong intersection, where worshippers leave garlands and hire classical dancers to give thanks.

sights.name: Benjakitti Forest Park
sights.note: A former tobacco factory turned wetland park, with elevated skywalks over marshes and a lake loop beside MRT Queen Sirikit Centre.
sights.hours: ~5:00 AM–9:00 PM daily (lake area to ~10:00 PM)

sights.name: Pak Khlong Talat (Flower Market)
sights.note: Bangkok's round-the-clock wholesale flower market, piled with marigold garlands, orchids and lotus buds; most vivid late at night.

railStations.name: Krung Thep Aphiwat Central Terminal
railStations.note: Bangkok's main intercity station since 2023 (formerly Bang Sue Grand): long-distance trains to Chiang Mai, the northeast (Nong Khai, Ubon) and the south (Hat Yai, Surat Thani, Padang Besar), plus the SRT Red Lines to Don Mueang Airport. Linked by underground walkway to MRT Blue Line Bang Sue.
railStations.hours: Station open ~4:30 AM–midnight. Long-distance trains run to individual timetables; Red Line ~5:30 AM–midnight.

railStations.name: Hua Lamphong Railway Station
railStations.note: The historic 1916 terminus beside Chinatown, now used by all Eastern Line trains (Pattaya, Aranyaprathet for the Cambodian border) and slow ordinary/commuter trains (e.g. to Ayutthaya); long-distance expresses moved to Krung Thep Aphiwat. Next to MRT Blue Line Hua Lamphong.
railStations.hours: Station open ~4:00 AM–11:00 PM. Trains run to individual timetables.

airports.name: Suvarnabhumi Airport
airports.transitNote: Airport Rail Link (from the terminal basement) to Makkasan (MRT Phetchaburi) in ~20 min and Phaya Thai (BTS) in ~26 min, 15–45 THB; shown on this map, but a separate system with its own fare (token or contactless card). Metered taxis ~45–60 min to Sukhumvit/Silom.
airports.hours: Airport Rail Link: first ~5:30 AM, last ~midnight. Late arrivals: public taxi rank (meter + 50 THB airport fee + tolls).

airports.name: Don Mueang International Airport
airports.transitNote: Bangkok's low-cost-airline airport (AirAsia, Nok Air, Thai Lion). SRT Dark Red Line from Don Mueang station (skybridge from Terminal 1) to Krung Thep Aphiwat in ~15 min, then MRT Blue Line from Bang Sue; 12–42 THB, contactless cards accepted (the Red Line is not on this map). Limousine Bus A1/A2 runs to BTS Mo Chit.
airports.hours: SRT Red Line: first ~5:30 AM, last ~midnight. Late arrivals: taxi rank (meter + 50 THB fee).
